idiom_name: null for nullable parameters, empty object expression for non-nullable ones
implementation_notes: Kotlin makes nullability part of the parameter type: a nullable parameter takes null as the placeholder, while a non-nullable collaborator needs an instance and the cheapest is an object expression (object : Collaborator { override fun log(e: String) = Unit }) or a small private class in the test source set. MockK fabricates one with mockk<Collaborator>(relaxed = true), but a relaxed mock returns defaults for every member and therefore behaves like a stub - it is a placeholder only while the path never touches it. Unused parameters are flagged by IDE inspections rather than the compiler and silenced with @Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER"); Kotlin's blank-identifier convention (_) applies to lambda parameters only, so an ignored constructor or method argument needs a comment or an underscore-prefixed name.
pitfalls: TODO() is a fail-fast guard, not an inert placeholder: it throws NotImplementedError, so a dummy written as TODO() makes the test depend on the parameter staying unused and turns a path change into a NotImplementedError.

A relaxed mock (mockk(relaxed = true)) answers every member with a default, so the 'never used' assumption is not enforced and interface changes go unnoticed; prefer an empty object expression where the interface is small.

A non-null assertion (!!) around a nullable placeholder reintroduces the escape the type system was there to prevent; type the placeholder against the interface instead of asserting on a nullable variable.
